title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-noah-wu
content:
Quick notes for PR review \u2014 KV cache + continuous batching refactor

Context:
- PR: gh://redwood-inference/serving-runtime#4721 (WIP) \u2014 refactors prefix/KV cache integration with batching layer.
- Goal: reduce redundant KV lookups during batched requests and enable partial prefix reuse across sequences of different lengths. Also unblock a follow-up to enable async cache warmups.
- Concern areas: correctness (cache hits/misses across shards), concurrency, perf regression risk for short seqs, memory overhead for new metadata.

High-level review checklist (start here for every pass):
- [ ] Tests: unit + integration coverage added? mock KV + multi-worker scenario
- [ ] Invariants: cache invalidation, TTL semantics preserved, model state unaffected
- [ ] Concurrency: race conditions on read-through and eviction paths
- [ ] Perf: microbenchmarks for short (<=8), medium (~64), long (~512) sequences
- [ ] Compatibility: fallback behavior if new cache disabled, config toggles documented
- [ ] Telemetry: new counter/gauge for cache hits/misses per-batch, latency histograms
- [ ] Docs: docstring + design note link to Confluence

Specific code areas to inspect:
1) batch_router.cpp / batch_router.h
- Line ~230: mergeBatchPrefixes() changed signature to take vector<PrefixMeta>. Ensure copy vs move semantics are correct \u2014 avoid copying large kv blobs. Suggest using const& for meta and explicit move for payloads when ownership transfers.
- Check comment about sequence-length bucketization: bucket boundaries changed from {16,64,256} to {8,32,128} \u2014 needs perf rationale. Add benchmark results in PR description for these thresholds.

2) kv_cache/kv_store.py (py shim)
- read_through() now returns (value, meta) tuple. Several callsites assume single value. Grep for .value or indexing. I found two callsites in runtime/scheduler.py that destructure differently \u2014 potential bug.
- Add assertion in read_through() to assert returned tuple length 2 in tests to catch binary mismatch.

3) scheduler/worker_pool.rs
- New locking around cache lookup: using Mutex<Cache> -> previously used RwLock. This could reduce concurrency on read-heavy workloads. Consider switching to a read-optimised approach (parking_lot::RwLock or dashmap) or use per-shard locks.
- TODO: run stress test (read-heavy) with 64 concurrent clients to check tail latency impact.

4) metrics & telemetry
- New metrics added: kv_batch_hits_total, kv_batch_misses_total, kv_batch_evictions_total. Good. Missing: per-batch latency histogram (quantiles) and tags for model_name + route. Request adding route label.

Testing notes
- Unit tests: add fakes for KV store that simulate partial prefix presence. Write tests for: 1) mixed-length batch where some items hit cache and others miss; 2) eviction during active batch; 3) disable-cache fallback.
- Integration: run on staging cluster with synthetic workload simulating single-token queries at 2000 rps and long-token streaming at 200 rps to ensure no regressions. Use canary route with 10% of traffic.

Perf experiments to include in PR description
- Baseline: master (commit abc123) with current thresholds
- Experiment A: new bucket thresholds + read_through tuple change
- Experiment B: new locking (RwLock) fallback
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 for token latency, throughput (tokens/s), CPU/GPU util, mem overhead per-worker.

Refactor ideas (follow-ups, not blocking):
- Split metadata from payload in cache entries to reduce copy sizes when only meta is needed (e.g., routing decisions).
- Expose a batched read interface on KV store to reduce syscall overhead when many cache keys requested at once.
- Consider introducing cache sharding by model + route to reduce lock contention (follow-up RFC).
- Async warmup: background worker to prefetch likely prefixes on model load or after canary rollout.

Small nit / formatting / doc TODOs
- Add a short note in the PR description about migration path for existing cache entries (if key format changes).
- Update config docs: default enabled=true? safer default is false until proven safe on staging.

Potential bugs I found in quick grep
- runtime/scheduler.py: line ~1120 calls kv.read_through(key) and then does if value is None: ... but with new tuple return, this will truthily pass. Needs to be updated to handle tuple or shim.
- batch_router.cpp: mergeBatchPrefixes uses std::move on local reference variable \u2014 dangling move risk.

Questions for author (put answers in PR description):
- Why change bucket boundaries? any model/workload traces that motivated this?
- Did you consider read-optimised lock (RwLock) instead of Mutex for the hot path?
- Memory overhead: how big are the meta objects per entry on average? estimate for 1M entries?

Action items (my follow-ups):
- [ ] Ask author to add microbenchmarks to PR description and run perf jobs (assign to Maya to run on staging).
- [ ] Add unit tests for tuple return shape (I'll draft tests later this week).
- [ ] Run quick grep to fix runtime/scheduler.py callsites (I'll open small PR if they want).
- [ ] Request telemetry label for route and model_name (Avery to add to metrics PR).

Scratch area / commands to run locally:
- perf harness: infra/perf/harness --workload=short-token --concurrency=64 --duration=5m --route=canary-kvtest
- run unit tests: tox -e py39 -- tests/kv_cache_tests.py::TestReadThrough
- quick grep: rg "read_through\(|mergeBatchPrefixes\(|kv_batch_hits_total" -n

Notes to self:
- Keep this PR review small and focused: block on correctness and telemetry, but make locking/opt changes a follow-up unless a clear regression is observed.
- If author prefers, propose a staged rollout: disable new cache on start and enable only via config once perf is validated in staging.

End of scratchpad.
